summary: James Darmesteter worked in Iranian and Central Asian studies and linguistics. He studied at the École Pratique des Hautes Études under Michel Bréal (~1872–1877), later holding posts there (~1877–1894) and at the Collège de France (1885–1894).

James Duerlinger is a scholar of philosophy and Buddhist studies. He studied at the University of Wisconsin-Madison (~1961–1964) under Sheldon Pollock and served as Professor Emeritus at the University of Iowa (~1971–2012).
James Dwight Dana studied at Yale College (~1830–1833). He spent his academic career at Yale University, holding a post there from ~1850 to 1892.
James Fergusson worked in history, archaeology, and Indology. He was educated at the Royal High School and held a post as a member of the Royal Asiatic Society of Great Britain and Ireland in 1840.
James Fieser works in philosophy and religious studies. He studied at Berea College and Purdue University (~1982–1986), and held a post at the University of Tennessee (~1992).
James G. Mullens specializes in religious studies and Buddhist studies. He earned his PhD from McMaster University and held a post at the University of Saskatchewan in 1989.

James H. Austin is a specialist in Buddhist studies. He trained under Katsujo Terayama and Nanrei Sohaku Kobori (~1974–1992), and held neurology posts at the University of Oregon/OHSU (~1960–1967) and the University of Colorado (~1967–1992).

James Hadley worked in linguistics and Indology, studying at Yale College and under Edward Elbridge Salisbury in 1849. He held posts as a tutor at Middlebury College (1845) and Professor of Greek at Yale University (1845–1872).

James Haughton Woods worked in Indology, philosophy, and religious studies. Educated at Harvard and Strasbourg, he studied under Paul Deussen, Arthur Venis, Mukunda Shastri Adkar, and Charles Rockwell Lanman before serving on Harvard University's faculty (~1903–1934).

James Ishmael Ford works in religious and Buddhist studies. He studied at Sonoma State University and the Pacific School of Religion (~1988–1991), and trained under Mel Weitsman, Hōun Jiyu-Kennett (~1970–1975), and John Tarrant.

James Kenneth Powell II specializes in Buddhist studies. He studied at Northwestern University, the University of Chicago under David Tracy, and the University of Wisconsin-Madison (PhD 1998) under Geshe Lhundub Sopa, Isshi Yamada, and David M. Knipe.

James L. Fitzgerald specializes in Indology and religious studies, having studied under J. A. B. van Buitenen. He held posts as Professor at the University of Tennessee (attested 2004–2006) and Das Professor of Sanskrit at Brown University (attested 2019).

James L. Taylor works in religious studies and Buddhist studies. He completed a PhD at Macquarie University by 1989 and served as Senior Lecturer in Anthropology at the University of Adelaide (attested 2014).

James Legge was a sinologist who studied at Aberdeen Grammar School, the University of Aberdeen (~1831–1835), and Highbury College (~1836–1839). He served as Professor at the University of Oxford beginning in 1876.

James Leibold specializes in sinology and Tibetology. He completed his PhD at the University of Southern California under Charlotte Furth, and held posts at the University of Melbourne and La Trobe University.

James Luther Adams worked in religious studies and philosophy. He studied at the University of Minnesota (~1920–1924), Harvard Divinity School (~1924–1927), and Harvard University (~1927–1930), later serving on the faculty at Harvard University (~1956–1968).

Indologist James Mallinson studied at Eton, SOAS, and Oxford under Alexis Sanderson. He held posts at SOAS (2013) and the University of Oxford, becoming Boden Professor of Sanskrit and Director of Graduate Studies at Wolfson College in 2023.

James Mark Shields works in Buddhist studies, philosophy, and Japanology. His posts include Associate Professor at Bucknell University (attested 2016) and Overseas Collaborative Researcher at the International Research Center for Japanese Studies (attested 2016).
James Matthew Baskind specializes in Buddhist studies and Japanology. He completed his Doctor of Philosophy at Yale University (attested 2006) under the supervision of Stanley Weinstein.

James McHugh works in Indology and religious studies. Educated at Cambridge, Oxford, and Harvard, his teachers included Lawrence J. McCrea, Anne E. Monius, and Parimal G. Patil. He held posts at Cornell University and the University of Southern California.
